what: of3t-recut job 3: the corrected trunk arm, and the control that says the shortcut is allowed.
note: this script is CPU arithmetic over three banked device arms; the AICLK and host_quiet of the two arms it composes are in DEV_RENORM_MODEL_N384_DELTA.json and DEV_RENORM_MODEL_N384_EXTERNAL.json

LINEARITY_CONTROL.what: the shortcut's result against the arm the device actually ran end to end on (cot_s, cot_z - delta)

reference_for_the_bar.what: || g_sonly + g_zonly - g_ctrl || / || g_ctrl || in this same setup, on the CPU reference. The device arm is bf16, so its own linearity residual is a measurement, not this number.

cancellation.what: the subtraction cancels two arms into a smaller result, so each arm's own rounding is amplified by this factor in the difference. The implied per-arm error is the residual divided by it, and it sits at bf16 scale, so this reads as the taped backward's own rounding rather than a wrong identity.

LINEARITY_CONTROL.verdict: the shortcut and the end-to-end arm differ by 2.208239e-02, far outside the float64 reference's own 6.435383e-15. On a bf16 taped backward the injection is linear only to its own rounding, so the SHORTCUT IS WITHDRAWN on device arms and the end-to-end arm is this row's corrected trunk. The repair itself is untouched: the float64 reference reproduces grads_f64_043 to 1.6952505222168708e-14 over all 2,736 tensors.

THE_CORRECTED_TRUNK_IS.why: the arm the device ran end to end on (cot_s, cot_z - delta), not the subtraction, because the subtraction failed its own control
